openPulls.title: Encode native actor operations from typed inputs, not JSON chat strings
openPulls.head: a4e4ef16a43dcee72bc2890bcfdc6d9c8b5aa1b2
openPulls.body:
## Original need and observed defect — 19 October 2026
The Leader asks us to prefer standard data formats and ActivityPub++ actor-to-actor transport rather than bespoke service/function message protocols. In the native world invocation path, FeltOS's `MudServer.invokeWorldAction()` currently serializes a structured `{verb,operation,input}` as JSON text before sending it. This RPC engine's `prepareMessage()` then guesses that `text.startsWith('{')` is a machine operation, reparses the text, and only *then* projects typed `metroplat.dispatch.arrival-material` SEN content through the existing ActivityPub / CloudEvents / A2A envelope. This is avoidable protocol inversion, and spoken JSON can be misclassified.

## Original source change (no parallel messaging stack)
- Add explicit `operationRequest` to the **original** `createActorClient.prepare/send` material contract; a caller supplies admitted structured `{verb, operation?, input, taskId?, paymentPayload?}`, never an encoded chat string.
- Reuse the **same existing** validation and projection: typed `metroplat.dispatch.arrival-material` -> SEN content-addressed bytes -> CloudEvents 1.0 JSON event inside ActivityStreams `Create` -> actor inbox over HTTPS. No second routing directory, queue, actor registry, socket, or authority ledger.
- Refuse simultaneous `text` and `operationRequest`, unknown fields, missing or non-JSON input, wrong operation NI, oversized typed material (>16 KiB), and payment without original task linkage before delivery.
- Existing text path remains temporarily intact for **as-yet-unmigrated** consumers. This is a bounded migration stage, not a claim that implicit JSON-text dispatch has been retired globally. The paired FeltOS consumer should move first and the fallback then be removed after enumerating/receiving remaining callers.
- Sender admission, recipient discovery, signing, per-effect receiver authority, durable request/result identity, retries and receiving remain owned by their existing ports. An encoded/transported event cannot grant an office, a capability, payment acceptance or executed effect.

## Source-backed receiving tests
`test/actor-typed-operation-transport.test.mjs` exercises actual projection through `readActorMessage`, checks the CloudEvents/A2A envelope and original structured request, and refuses ambiguous/invalid/oversized requests before a network effect. These are **authored tests, not yet an executed receipt**.

## Downstream/rollout
Paired FeltOS consumer branch: `red-cup-engineering/feltos:feat/native-typed-actor-operation-port-20261019`.
This Systems engine remains the upstream serializer owner; FeltOS owns the world command and ActivityPub service owns delivery. Before receiving either change into a deployed host: run this package's native test suite; release the exact candidate; update the original FeltOS dependency/lock through its native package workflow; run existing `addressed-method-effects` two-host signed effect/custody test plus new method-port test; receive a real actor request/result on the consuming FeltOS/MUD instance. Do not switch the consumer to an unreleased engine version.

Reference: [MetroPlat typed messages #9](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/metroplat/issues/9); [coordination standards #28](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/metroplat/issues/28). CloudEvents [specification](https://github.com/cloudevents/spec), W3C [ActivityPub](https://www.w3.org/TR/activitypub/) and current A2A transport distinguish envelope/delivery from authorization/acceptance. The A2A-shaped data inside ActivityPub is not claimed to be a standalone A2A 1.0 wire-compatible endpoint.

**Verified here:** GitHub branch + source/test commits exist. **Unverified:** local Node tests, dependency-backed test run, published package, FeltOS installed selection, deployed federation and independent consumer receiving.

openIssues.title: SEV-1: Stop package-only PR fabrication from deleting repository roots; recover 13 source trees
openIssues.body:
## 2026-10-19 follow-on — PR65 source and CI capacity boundary

The current original Systems Fabrication safety candidate is [PR #65](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/computer-systems-fabrication-engineering-services-section/pull/65) at head `3b86651a2ed0e5fc03a0ded8d86f87a0fea81164` (the previous `e267dc32` link records an earlier commit). It changes precisely the original `content/handoffs/frankenstein-disassembly/tools/repair-closure.sh`, its existing `test/repair-closure-handoff-script.test.mjs`, and its package `receivingTests` selection, preserving the previously merged #64 manifest-only before/after diff guard. It isolates repairs from shared temporary directories, preserves actual source HEAD/default branch and refuses failed push/PR as success. The candidate remains **draft**, not deployed.

The native private GitHub Actions [run 39296931877](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/computer-systems-fabrication-engineering-services-section/actions/runs/39296931877) returned failure with no retrievable job steps. Multiple prior *main* runs of the same workflow likewise failed, and [GitHub Engineering P0 #7](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/github-engineering-services-section/issues/7) documents exhausted private GitHub-hosted capacity with CircleCI Free App/project receiving still owed. Do NOT silently resubmit private hosted workflows or count absent steps as a source test failure; no paid minutes or capacity activation is approved. PR65's original native engine-backed test and independently received operator call still need a working lawful execution path. This incident does not authorize rerunning 16 destructive batch candidates; the 13 restored default trees and held 3 rejected PRs must be preserved.

---

## Confirmed cause and live producer repair — 2026-10-19 (updates the historical hypothesis below)

The destructive October 19 `Publish only the package's own files` batch has a confirmed **original shell author**: `red-cup-engineering/computer-systems-fabrication-engineering-services-section/content/handoffs/frankenstein-disassembly/tools/repair-closure.sh`. The original tool cloned repositories with `git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout`, materialized only their `package.json` paths, then ran `git commit -a`. Git correctly treated every tracked file missing from the incomplete worktree as a requested deletion. This was **not** an observed defect in the package-closure derivation, `check-section-repositories`, or the GitHub landing composition's existing `base_tree` implementation. See the exact old/new shell diff and its original local bare-Git regression in [Systems Fabrication #64](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/computer-systems-fabrication-engineering-services-section/pull/64) (merged at `46411708e6d4da1bb841a7288d37bbd6dae3752d`).

**Original effect boundary already repaired in `main` by #64:** the actual script uses `--changed-paths-file` and stages exactly the named manifest files, with `--assert-repair-only` before commit and over the committed range before push; a mismatched or deleted path is refused. The separately owned CLI's invariant is manifest changes, not source-tree exclusion. The recovery commits and three held, nonmerged mass-deletion PRs recorded below remain preserved.

**Current improvement candidate:** [Systems Fabrication PR #65](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/computer-systems-fabrication-engineering-services-section/pull/65), head `e267dc32894c5b7f68212b0d1f80943d358e64bf`, modifies only that original script, its original tests, and the original package's `receivingTests` selection. It removes a hard-coded ephemeral scratch root and shared destructive clone directory; isolates each repair, verifies origin source/base and candidate, and surfaces checkout/repair/staging/commit/push/PR failures without phantom success. It exercises repeated candidate construction and push-versus-PR boundaries against local bare-Git fixtures. **The candidate remains draft**; its complete dependency-backed native test suite and independent operator receiving are not yet observed, so it must not be represented as a deployed or integrated fix.

**Outstanding incident closure:** verify the active installed operator actually selects the safe original script; independently execute native tests and one bounded real *manifest-only* repair with exact source-tree readback; receive or withhold the incomplete Filum source transfer; preserve the 13 recovered source trees and three rejected destructive candidates. No wholesale re-execution of the original 16-repository batch. Do not claim that closing a GitHub source PR is itself installed-source or downstream release receiving. The earlier "strong hypothesis" section below remains as time-stamped initial investigation, not current causal uncertainty.

---

# Incident: package-local publish repair landed repository-root deletions

**Date:** 2026-10-19 UTC. **Scope:** 561 Group, Lenticule Science, Red Cup Engineering, Coesite Operations, Causeway Services. **Classification:** source-tree integrity / destructive Git authoring / same-work recovery; **no authority, funds, deployments or customer Work granted by this issue.**

## Observable defect, not a speculative diagnosis

The source-owned `check-section-repositories --repair-published-closure` improvement from [Systems Fabrication #57](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/computer-systems-fabrication-engineering-services-section/pull/57) and [#58](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/computer-systems-fabrication-engineering-services-section/pull/58) is supposed to narrow the `files` array in **the actual installable package's** `package.json`. Its inspected code computes `publishedClosureRepairs`, reads the current manifest and writes that manifest; it does **not** intentionally delete files in the owning Git tree.

Nevertheless, a 16-PR batch entitled `Publish only the package's own files` was created. **13 were merged; three were not merged** (561-group/561-group-services-section#190, red-cup-engineering/engineering-services-section#126, lenticule-science/science-services-section#192). Numerous PRs changed thousands of paths yet added only a few lines. For example, Science #193 removed its README, AGENTS, workflows, research and 31,084 tracked paths. This was an invalid translation of package distribution scope into source-repository scope.

**Strong hypothesis, still to prove:** a PR/commit fabrication path constructed a new Git root tree from only selected working files or changed blobs without preserving the existing HEAD tree (e.g. missing `base_tree` in Git Trees API, or staging missing paths from an incomplete checkout). Merely naming `--repair-published-closure` in the commit message does not prove that this CLI itself generated the deletions. The existing native [GitHub landing composition](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/github-engineering-services-section/blob/main/src/landing-composition.mjs) already uses `POST /git/trees` with `base_tree`; examine and reuse that implementation rather than invent a second Git writer. Record which exact producer authored these specific full-root trees before changing its authority or code.

## Recovery already performed — original tree preserved with normal descendant commits

Each recovery commit has the erroneous merge as its first parent and names the **exact pre-merge tree**, avoiding a force-push or rewrite. Its public/private accessible immutable PR and commit locations follow:

| Erroneous merged PR | Observed deletion scale | Corrective normal commit |

| [causeway-services/koios-news-data#5](https://github.com/causeway-services/koios-news-data/pull/5) | 8,320 files / 905,030 lines | [2cbd0d43a339](https://github.com/causeway-services/koios-news-data/commit/2cbd0d43a3394b4f7e2412c672dbc6cc74a2db9a) |
| [red-cup-engineering/2026-08-03-red-cup-engineering-corpus#1](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/2026-08-03-red-cup-engineering-corpus/pull/1) | 7,051 files / 1,112,067 lines | [0ebf2e264391](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/2026-08-03-red-cup-engineering-corpus/commit/0ebf2e264391875ef078486eab2946b88d77d647) |

| [lenticule-science/semiotics-services-section#4](https://github.com/lenticule-science/semiotics-services-section/pull/4) | 39 files / 1,322 lines | [77059bea6cdf](https://github.com/lenticule-science/semiotics-services-section/commit/77059bea6cdf9258a08563f213fe21b2210f7c9e) |
| [coesite-operations/computer-operations-services-section#5](https://github.com/coesite-operations/computer-operations-services-section/pull/5) | 13 files / 325 lines | [9ca390209ca5](https://github.com/coesite-operations/computer-operations-services-section/commit/9ca390209ca5d45dd576b340e4fb956b5d8749b8) |
| [561-group/561-group-computer-services-section#7](https://github.com/561-group/561-group-computer-services-section/pull/7) | 534 files / 67,104 lines | [747621276e6f](https://github.com/561-group/561-group-computer-services-section/commit/747621276e6f24617fde7eb2c0510375fb4aba29) |
| [causeway-services/public-news-media-services-section#1](https://github.com/causeway-services/public-news-media-services-section/pull/1) | 1,795 files / 201,841 lines; also reversed incomplete Filum submodule receiving | [bfe54efe563c](https://github.com/causeway-services/public-news-media-services-section/commit/bfe54efe563cfa77f46d1e44e98bd6a371957cc9) |

Current main-ref readback showed all recovery heads at the expected commits, except **Science** which subsequently advanced one valid commit and retained the restored README and tree as an ancestor. News Media had additionally accepted a later `Extract filum-561-group` commit: its proposed submodule pointed to `causeway-services/filum-561-group@8d8da048`, whose recursively read tree had **only one `package.json`**, whereas the original `sites/filum.561.group` directory had **267 entries**; the follow-up commit was also reversed by the normal News Media recovery to preserve those original sources pending genuine receiving. Do not reintroduce a gitlink until the new owner actually holds those contents and all former sibling submodule declarations survive.

## Change the responsible original software, not a checklist

1. **Find exact tree producer**. Inspect the GitHub PR head commits and working authoring calls for this batch. Compare the actual produced tree entries with base-commit trees. Determine whether the defect was omitted `base_tree`, sparse/worktree staging, a gitlink conversion path, or another mechanism. The correlation with the CLI title is insufficient to blame the CLI parser.
2. **Repair the existing native GitHub source-commit operation**. For a change to an existing repository, bind immutable default-branch SHA, read its tree, overlay exactly the intended path/blob/mode changes on that base tree, and parent the commit to that source. Refuse root-only replacement, undefined base-tree claims, missing tracked content, and unintended gitlink conversion. A repository-formation operation that genuinely starts empty is a **different typed effect** requiring its own source identity.
3. **Repair the actual package continuation**. `--repair-published-closure` must yield a bounded set of changed `*/package.json` files. GitHub candidate creation must not publish deleted Git source or remove unselected children just because they should not appear in an npm tarball. Reject any candidate that touches paths outside the declared manifest changes *before the PR is offered for merger*. Do not disable legitimate package ownership checks.
4. **Exercise two genuine receiving counterexamples in the original tests**: (a) a repo with `README.md`, `.gitmodules`, 200-plus source files, child packages and one offending package `files` array receives one manifest change while all untouched Git tree entries remain byte-identical; (b) an incompletely materialized checkout / erroneous Git tree with only a manifest refuses rather than becoming a replacement root. A separate true empty-repo formation remains possible under its own creator API. Use current provider/consumer tests, not a new audits service.
5. **Repair the Filum source transfer at its owner**: compare each former `sites/filum.561.group` relative path and exact blob with the *new owner's* installed and Git source; preserve all unique files and retained outputs before replacing the donor with a submodule. Mere ownership of a package.json is not a successful extraction.
6. **Independent receiving**: repeat one real package-publish closure repair against an actual nonempty repository, read back exact Git source changes and package tarball membership, and prove the original source remains complete. Native CI, package publication, host receiving and external use are separate observations.

**Safety conditions:** Never force-reset main to repair these events; preserve erroneous commits for forensic history. Never merge or rerun the batch unchanged. Do not spend money, publish artifacts, redeploy, alter branch protection or claim another office approved a change. Do not assume all downstream installed services observed the invalid intermediate tree; check affected release readers if needed.

## Completion criteria

The original source-commit writer is corrected with a tested causal counterexample; all 13 restored source trees remain recoverable on default branches; the three nonmerged mass-delete PRs stay unmerged; valid package-local repairs are independently sourced and testable; and the incomplete Filum migration is correctly received or explicitly withheld. Close this incident only for verified software and source custody, not for rhetorical assurances.

- **Original private consuming repository:** [Git Services PR #75](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/git-services-section/pull/75), merged `d87c898d43276baeb4f61b27906bea1a6f66a776`. Removed its sole exhausted private hosted `.github/workflows/chatgpt-recovery-custody.yml`, its unapproved `cloudbuild.yaml`, and provider-specific GCP regression. The new owner test was executed by the actual public CI (included in 128/128); private Git Services' no-billing guard was independently run in a native Node fixture (**2/2**). **These tests validate configuration/source mechanics, NOT CircleCI private execution or full Git Services suite.**

# Account and GitHub App exist; original private project/execution still required

The original account and installed App are now independently distinguished from private project execution. This session has no authenticated CircleCI operation, and the current GitHub credential cannot read the App's exact repository selection. Preserve the existing selected grant; do not reinstall the App or manufacture provider readiness. An authorized existing account actor with the required native access must:

1. Verify the **existing** CircleCI GitHub App installation **172175362** selects the public red-cup-engineering/continuous-delivery-services-section configuration source and original private red-cup-engineering/git-services-section checkout source. Exact repository selection remains unread here; selected access is not evidence that those two repositories are absent or present. Keep the existing grant and financial boundary; do not repeat signup/installation or expand permissions without an actual required source grant and its authority.
2. Create a **Git Services** CircleCI project, selecting public CD `.circleci/config.yml` from protected `main` as **configuration source** and original private Git Services as **checkout source**. If tests fail, repair their actual original source and rerun only with a concrete failure receipt. If the GitHub App cannot read one source, qualify/fix the real app grant rather than weakening source checks.
4. Then receive a **second** Red Cup private repository with a genuinely runnable original `npm run verify` under the same Engineering configuration and independently read its provider receipt before closing P0.

**Status:** Existing account and active GitHub App installation are established; no CircleCI project, Free-credit balance, private runner job, or full Git Services result has been observed. **P0 remains OPEN.** The previous Google Cloud Build research and source remains in the generic Continuous Delivery Engineering owner for separate authorized consumers, but is not part of this private CI recovery.

openIssues.title: SEV-1: ChatGPT-Web scheduled execution leaves orphaned work and incurs premium cleanup cost
openIssues.body:
# SEV-1 / Corporate production incident — scheduled ChatGPT-Web partial execution and accumulating unfinished work

**Status: OPEN / CONTAINED, NOT FIXED.** The Leader first paused all ChatGPT Scheduled Tasks, then explicitly authorized **only two** existing circulatory focuses: ChatGPT-Web → Semioverse source intake and a separate source-to-Semioverse improvement focus. Both must make at most one external tool call per scheduled run. No other focus may be reactivated without new Leader instruction. This is a material operating-cost and mission-continuity incident for the 561 Group, not a source-code feature request or permission request.

## Controlling operator evidence (Leader's longitudinal observation)

Across **thousands of scheduled turns over several days**, the Leader observed that **the first external tool call succeeds most of the time; subsequent calls in the same scheduled execution fail most of the time**. Treat that longitudinal report as an operating fact for containment. Do not substitute a successful manual conversation or one successful scheduled experiment for it. The exact platform-internal reason is not yet known.

Failure chain: a scheduled run makes a persistent first-step mutation (issue, branch, PR, provisional record), subsequent action(s) are denied, and the unfinished state is abandoned; later invocations repeat the cycle. The fleet has thereby accumulated unmerged/unreceived objects and shifted scientific, engineering, public-service and revenue work into **premium-use-credit-funded human cleanup**. This is production harm even if an individual first tool response said SUCCESS. No invented numerical incident counts or spending amounts.

Directly observed failures have included `CHATGPT_HARNESS_POLICY_BLOCK` and `This tool call was blocked by OpenAI's safety checks. Please double check what you're sending.` before GitHub dispatch. Interactive tool success is **not** scheduled-context receiving. Distinguish refusal from provider errors and from intentional safety boundaries; do not bypass genuine platform refusals.

## Independent corroboration and platform scope (as of 2026-10-11)

- OpenAI currently documents that Scheduled Tasks can act through connected apps, subject to permissions/approval: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10291617-scheduled-tasks-in-chatgpt
- Multiple outside users reported blocked scheduled writes to Gmail, Sheets, Trello and GitHub, sometimes with the same safety-check message, while interactive actions succeeded: https://community.openai.com/t/regression-scheduled-tasks-safety-checks-block-authorized-gmail-sends-and-google-sheets-writes/1403242
- Another report captures scheduled GitHub-write failure and unexpected automatic recurrence disablement, documented separately from the 561 Group: https://community.openai.com/t/chatgpt-scheduled-tasks-fail-to-write-to-github-and-automatically-disable-themselves-after-failed-executions-without-user-authorization/1404882
- A cross-provider bug filed 2026-10-10 requests OpenAI host-owned traces and diagnosis: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52872
- Earlier multi-call regression reports exist, but involve different model configurations; do **not** claim they prove this root cause: https://community.openai.com/t/the-new-chatgpt-5-5-instant-broke-multi-step-app-mcp-tool-calls/1385257
- OpenAI's Oct 5–6 Work incident explicitly noted scheduled tasks *may* be affected, but was closed Oct 6; neither that incident nor its resolution explains later failures: https://status.openai.com/incidents/mysmq298

## Containment and operating constraints

1. **Exactly the two Leader-authorized circulation focuses may run**; the other existing ChatGPT tasks remain paused, including the extra CIO recovery task. No autonomous reactivation, creation of substitutes, or hourly experiments.
2. **Do not dispatch multi-step ChatGPT tool workflows from Scheduled.** For any future authorized restart, the scheduled invocation must be able to deliver a worthwhile, independently complete outcome using at most one ordinary external call, or merely analyze and deliver a useful result without an external mutation. No hidden multi-tool batching as an evasion.
3. **No first-step orphan creation**: no standalone branch, issue, PR, ticket, task or new ledger entry whose value depends on a second call. Updating an existing, correctly owned authoritative resource is preferable only when that specific single operation can stand alone and has appropriate custody.
4. **Do not attempt user-directed N=1 tests to dispute the longitudinal report**; no periodic retries, "safety policy" prompt incantations, permission re-approval rituals, or additional infrastructure merely to instrument ChatGPT failures.
5. Use existing 561 operational services and runbooks where there is a real, compatible single-call interface, rather than fabricating a new agent framework. An earlier proposed native GitHub executor is **source-only**, not independently verified as a deployed fix. Do not pretend it solves the hosted OpenAI policy path.
6. Preserve the original corporate circulation purpose: Leader/Board/Group/Public requirements → Science → Engineering → Operations → independent receiving; prioritize restoration of productive research, customer delivery, publishing, services and revenue over process machinery.
7. Existing 561 Group branch-cleanup custody is https://github.com/561-group/561-group-services-section/issues/71; reconcile by original work identity and source before integrating/discarding anything. This incident owns the generating failure, not a duplicate branch-cleanup queue.

## 2026-10-11 implemented containment (source and provider distinction)

- Scheduler provider was observed to drift back to multi-call prompts and to enable an extra CIO task. That third task was paused again; both authorized tasks were rewritten with a hard one-external-call budget. This protects against starting work the observed harness frequently cannot complete, but does **not** repair OpenAI's dispatch policy.
- The canonical Group scheduler roster now records `active_focus_ids` of the intake and improvement tasks: [commit 6225f8e](https://github.com/561-group/561-group-services-section/commit/6225f8e4abc03bbacc2eecbbbfa38b1d8865b0ff). The existing auditor rejects a third enabled circulation focus: [commit f161f56](https://github.com/561-group/561-group-services-section/commit/f161f56e0abb0c10241632943e6cc4303e16fc63). Real Node regression tests were added and repaired; [Actions CI run 38187220365](https://github.com/561-group/561-group-services-section/actions/runs/38187220365) passed.
- The existing first-party GitHub review-operation source now has a read-only dependency-free test workflow. [Commit 0315417](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/github-engineering-services-section/commit/031541726137aa5fb458c4a587b9c31dd36c900d), [CI passed](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/github-engineering-services-section/actions/runs/38186865120). This is not evidence that its native operations are installed on Cold Red Gate.
- Source review shows Cold Red Gate `deployment/instance.json` currently does not list the review-operation provider; `sources.json` also lacks the `github-engineering-services-section` source. Integrating those requires real host-held credentials, selected source/dependency lock, capability admission, and independent runtime receiving—not a blind package pin.
- The native `metroplat_harness_hook_event_admit` operation explicitly refuses arbitrary `PulseEgress` with `harness:mcp`: MCP participation requires `SessionStart` or `SessionEnd` plus the real client session id. This is a contract refusal, not a missing ChatGPT approval. The first circulation task uses one `metroplat_world_command say`, which establishes only room testimony, **not** typed work admission/independent receiving.

## Correct engineering boundary and vendor escalation

**The apparent pre-provider refusal is in OpenAI's scheduled execution/harness control plane**, outside the authority of a Red Cup repository patch. Route this report to OpenAI Support's Scheduled Tasks/Work/Connectors/safety-execution owners. Ask them to inspect **existing** affected run traces, not ask the Leader to recreate thousands of failures or spend premium credits on probes:

- per-run model and execution mode; first versus subsequent tool dispatch sequence; tool availability/registration between calls;
- exact predispatch decision, stage/reason code, effective app permissions in *scheduled* context, approval-state handling, and whether the provider was invoked;
- task/run identifiers, exact Central/UTC timestamps, job continuation budget/runtime constraints, and whether a failed action automatically disables a recurrence;
- vendor-supported unattended alternatives with explicit capability limitations and a concrete fix/incident reference.
- Treat credit expenditure, foregone work, manual cleanup time and increased orphan count as **incident costs**, not user-error support questions. Seek consideration of affected paid usage without inventing reimbursement rights.

Official support path: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6614161-how-can-i-contact-support (support chat bubble). The user may give exact private task IDs/account details there; do not place them in public issues.

## Exit criteria (no N=1 theatre)

This incident remains OPEN until the scheduled-execution limitation is acknowledged and resolved by the responsible platform **or** an existing, production-received, supported single-call circulation mechanism safely delivers recurring real outcomes with no orphan-producing dependency. One interactive success or isolated scheduled success is not acceptance. The Leader decides when and whether to resume tasks. Separate source correctness, deploy/run, tool availability, and independent institutional receiving. Track reduced orphan production, completed customer-facing effects, and avoided premium cleanup burden, rather than counting new code or issue volume.

---

## Prior technical evidence and scope (retained for provenance)

## Control-plane evidence — 2026-10-09

An explicitly authorized interactive diagnostic established the GitHub side is healthy:

- authenticated GitHub user: `emsenn`
- ChatGPT GitHub app-specific permission: **Allow all actions**
- GitHub App installed with `repository_selection=all` on `561-group`, `causeway-services`, `coesite-operations`, `lenticule-science`, `red-cup-engineering`, and related orgs
- `561-group/x402-boundary-reference` reports admin + push
- diagnostic branch in `561-group/561-group-opportunity-services-section` successfully exercised:
  - create branch
  - create file
  - update file
  - delete file
  - create draft PR
  - close/update PR
- diagnostic PR was closed unmerged and probe file deleted

Therefore the recurring pre-dispatch blocks are not evidence of GitHub auth, installation, repository ACL, or provider runtime failure.

## Required behavior

1. Autonomous/scheduled runs must distinguish pre-provider ChatGPT action-safety blocks from GitHub/provider failures.
2. Routine internal mutations in already-owned 561 repos (branch/file/commit/issue/comment/PR/review/labels/workflow rerun) should use the existing standing authority without requiring per-action user confirmation.
3. Merge/deploy/default-branch/org-security/publication/spend/secrets/cross-principal effects remain separately gated.
4. On any failure, classify earliest layer and repair that layer rather than ending the run.
5. If a harness block persists, do not bypass it with lower-level actuators; continue independent work and retain the incident until a normal GitHub mutation succeeds from the affected autonomous context.
6. Build a regression/preflight that can be run from scheduled ChatGPT-Web contexts and records: app permission, installation coverage, repository permission, attempted mutation class, whether dispatch left ChatGPT, provider receipt, and side effect.

## Acceptance

- At least one scheduled ChatGPT-Web office run performs a normal bounded source mutation and PR/issue workflow in an owned repo under the same GitHub connection without a harness block.
- Failure provenance correctly distinguishes client validation, harness policy, connector routing, auth/ACL, provider validation/runtime, and readback mismatch.
- Recurrent GitHub blocker receipts no longer terminate the office shift when other repair/execution branches remain.

openPulls.title: Expose read-only sealed target checks before receiving
openPulls.head: 1f94535017573c8c6fcb789d7e9d2f3df0372915
openPulls.body:
Guix's current registry-native machine comparison needs to inspect a completed LAGOON product's sealed target binding without invoking receiving. This adds `check-target CHANNELS STORE PROFILE TARGET` to the existing Guile driver, reusing the receive/rollback predicate and checking registered, canonical store custody before and after reading.

The complete [source-owned requirement](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/computer-deployment-engine/blob/1f94535017573c8c6fcb789d7e9d2f3df0372915/content/text/documents/specifications/read-only-target-check.md) defines inputs, observed JSON fields, refusals, trusted-channel prerequisite, preserved target/role semantics and qualification. CHANNELS is previously authenticated trusted Scheme with no effects or stdout output; the existing reader evaluates it. LAGOON's check bypasses profile creation, retention roots, activation and the activation lease. It is neither a sandbox nor source provenance, machine acceptance or deployment permission.

Source custody:
- Original base: `c40ef8cc715fc61831dd298308198c76f0cd694a`.
- Previously reviewed head: `abf95bbb0028b1677b8f3611b9736f95c98aa8e4`.
- Incorporated accepted main: `ddba5d59f9237ca10ce1b2568215b512dda506ae`.
- Resulting qualified head: `1f94535017573c8c6fcb789d7e9d2f3df0372915`; tree `654dee5d72e6768943a13a53442b05385c21a367`.
- Reviewed driver `a6de146cb772934df82daeb39d3a5ef0a399c46f`, test `067fd59225046ebd867bbd0e0089e4a5fc5e1772`, specification `35b7168436283d1093180c85ecbf0f8b2b48cfb6` are unchanged. Hosted commit/tree/blob readback completed.

Qualification:
- Complete declared public source suite: 321 Guile/Guix assertions and 25 Node tests passed; exit 0.
- Exact extracted packed artifact: same complete suite passed, exit 0. Both runs used the sole producer runner and the existing owner supplier closure whose installed/source lock SHA256 is `02368770d0677869e52b24ee135d2dd9fa43a2b2e98c7bd9140c3a774d20a143`. Manifest, lock and configuration hashes stayed unchanged. This is not an independent frozen installation.
- PNPM pack succeeded: 63,516 bytes, 27 files; SHA256 `7050d598d8def85a618be97aceb6aee016dd9c9c362a993aa2603f16c4fac0db`; integrity `sha512-eLtO41VcH2TvswCDTfuh9ZNK5LbtvZKurShqfaqjdeF5LGDk7f/lU3+f2Co2aurmX+McGarS1MOt0ZwEfFqHqg==`.
- Strict byte audit returned 1: only package.json differs. Separate reconciliation returned 0: PNPM reordered the scripts key/formatting without changing any parsed manifest value or test command; the other 26 files and modes match exact source.
- Independent reviewer `/root/independent_contract_review` accepted the final head, read the source/artifact results and independently hashed the archive. The trusted-CHANNELS finding is resolved; no remaining blocking source finding. Reviewer performed no tests or edits.

Ready for review; **not qualified for merge yet**. The exact [CD contract, README lines 630–645 at b697963](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/continuous-delivery-services-section/blob/b697963f336ed5c457e2f68e98111ee325213148/README.md#L630-L645) states: “Merge: with a merge commit, by whoever made the change, once the change test reports no-regression.” Executable driver and test-selection changes exclude this PR from both approved source-only exceptions. Local checks/artifact qualification cannot replace that explicit prerequisite. No machine verdict exists for this resulting tree; no protection or gate has been changed.

Current failed/unmet native contract and enabling event:
- [Guix receiver at c54c650](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/guix-machine-release-service/blob/c54c65064e678963c00e36edcded771ac473988c/scripts/receive-pull-requests.mjs#L395-L400) returns `outcome: incomplete`, `stage: native-product-receiving`, `runtimeAcceptance: false`, reason: “Native base/candidate fabrication, original engineering obligations and target interfaces have not been received.” This is source readback of the retained v3 route, not a newly executed held request.
- Enabling event: the Guix owner qualifies the current registry-native paired binding from genuine Code source/consumer/committed-lock/frozen-install/runtime evidence to actual immutable LAGOON products, receives original engineering/target obligations, and records an exact-candidate no-regression verdict. The historical common-root v3 route and this target check cannot be relabeled as that binding.
- [Guix#101](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/guix-machine-release-service/issues/101) / [BCF#765](https://github.com/561-group/bare-cedar-fog/issues/765) remain open. Paired Code evidence/custody was requested from existing BCF writer task `01a14777-efa5-7633-896a-df9e6cdb001d`, under existing `operating-engineering-release-and-recovery` Work; no duplicate install/runner or native allocation was created.
- Separate native-allocation observation remains unverified: automatic approval review rejected `operations agency` because it was not a clearly supported read-only query and side effects were ambiguous. It was not retried or bypassed. A verified supported read-only interface or explicit authorization for that exact operation enables this observation; it does not waive the machine gate.

openIssues.title: Make native test fabrication explicit and capacity-admitted outside ordinary source QA
openIssues.body:
The default package test runner includes `guix repl -L src -- test/deployment-lifecycle-test.scm`. That fixture calls `build-derivations` (line43) to build two real applications, so an ordinary source validation command can silently materialize native store dependencies and substitute downloads.

Witness2026-10-19: while qualifying PR54, the declared full test command reached this fixture under an existing BCF physical-storage/GC hold. It downloaded native substitutes before the receiving operator identified and stopped its exact own QA cohort. No host release formation, profile promotion, copy or production service activation occurred; existing GC and production custody were preserved. The41 activation/control cases,11 declaration cases and separately isolated native systemd old-interpreter/new-ExecStop bridge remain distinct valid results. This is a test-carrier failure, not permission to weaken the release gate.

Required owner repair: give ordinary source/control QA and real native fixture fabrication explicit separate entrances; make native fabrication require the existing source-owned finite capacity/storage admission and managed operation handle. Keep the actual generated-unit/lifecycle integration coverage through that admitted carrier. Missing admission must refuse before any native materialization, including missing-substitute acquisition. Do not blanket-skip the fixture or change assertions just to obtain green output.

Receive both paths: default source QA must prove zero native build/substitution effects; the explicitly admitted native path must still fabricate the two fixture outputs and receive their original PartOf/Wants/unit-byte invariants. Exercise refusal under a storage hold and retention of original unknown/failed operation custody. Source-owned skills/runbooks must route callers to the correct entrance. This is a bounded follow-up to PR54 and issue48, without retargeting the active tagged-selector bootstrap.

openIssues.title: Deploy qualified immutable host releases instead of default-branch landings
openIssues.body:
Production deployment currently follows default-branch landing reports and also promotes latest main on controller startup. This makes ordinary integration a production rollout decision and can select sources newer than the triggering event.

Leader requirement (2026-10-19): move from "shit monitors main to deploy stuff" to "proper release tags" and current industry practice.

Required behavior: each host owns published immutable SemVer releases. Its tag resolves to the exact host commit; a checksum-bound release asset binds the composition, host, agency and qualified immutable native product. Form and test that product once, then promote the same artifacts through the existing native receiving, fresh lease/live-state, capacity and health/rollback controls. Main/package integration may continue preparing candidates but cannot authorize a production deployment. Startup/reconnect reconciles release identities only. Duplicates do not reactivate; uncertain attempts and explicit rollback hold until reconciled. Mutable/moved tags or changed assets refuse. Preserve existing state, credentials, alternative explicit manual recovery, source lineage and unrelated work.

Implementation owners: computer-deployment-engine product/controller and Bare Cedar Fog machine declaration. Existing PR13 remains a separate held target-check proposal. Source acceptance, registry publication, installed controller, first tagged release and useful production receiving are separate outcomes.

This issue is authored by Codex acting in engineering execution; emsenn is the authenticated repository account, not the author of this text.
